# CT abdomen/pelvis acute — Dr Fiona McAllister (fictional)

Consultant GI and emergency radiologist at a fictional district general hospital. Fuller but economical prose, one unheaded paragraph per organ group under capitalised colon headers (CLINICAL DETAILS / TECHNIQUE / FINDINGS / CONCLUSION).
Prefers "unremarkable" for organs and "free intraperitoneal gas"; fixed one-line technique. Numbered conclusion, then an unnumbered "Recommend [surgical|urgent surgical|urology] review." on abnormal studies.
Leads FINDINGS with the bowel paragraph when the acute pathology is bowel or appendix, rewrites that paragraph without its stock negatives for obstruction/perforation, and writes finding-linked negatives (perforation, closed loop, ischaemia) next to the finding.
